correctness.rationale: The kernel domain is the infinite (q+1)-regular tree, integer q>=2, 0<r<1 and real b. For r below q^{-1/2}, an exact bounded adjacency resolvent and the full spectral interval give both sharp inequalities. At equality, an exact positivity-matrix factorization and two-by-two principal minors prove the one-sided interval. Above equality, normalized distant minors tend to a strictly negative squared quantity when b is nonzero, while the pure exponential remains positive by a tree Hilbert embedding. Exact symbolic checker reproduced the endpoint and critical identities and a rational negative minor; no finite experiment is promoted to an infinite proof.

value.rationale: This natural first-order deformation of exponential tree covariances has a sharp and usable complete coefficient cone for every finite degree and damping base. The admissible interval changes from two-sided to one-sided at square-summable radial decay, and then collapses to the undeformed exponential. Those global spectral and matrix-sign mechanisms explain a structural threshold, not an arbitrary low-parameter computation.
